title: English Language Paper 2 Writing – Mock Paper 3
instructions: This paper consists of two parts, Part A and Part B. Answer Question 1 in Part A and ONE question from Part B.
Part A: write about 200 words. Part B: write about 400 words.
Do not use your real name. If you need a name, use 'Chris Wong'.
You may use the information given in a question, but do not simply copy it.

partA.role: a teenager who has just tried a beginners' climbing session
partA.audience: young people who read the OutThere HK review website
partA.prompt:
You recently went to a beginners' session at Clip In Climbing, a new indoor climbing gym in Kwun Tong. OutThere HK, a website where young people review places to go in their free time, invites visitors to post reviews using the form below. You have also kept the gym's advertisement.

Write a review of about 200 words for the website. In your review, you should:
contentPoints: describe your visit and what happened in the beginners' session
explain the ratings you gave in the four areas of the form
say who you would recommend the gym to, and suggest one thing it could improve

input.description: Left: a small advertisement with a cartoon climbing wall, a 'NOW OPEN' banner, a short list of what the Beginners' Taster includes, prices and opening hours. Right: a review form from the OutThere HK website with boxes for name, date of visit and review title, four rows of rating icons (five empty stars each) labelled Staff, Safety, Price and Facilities, and a large text box for the review.
items: Advertisement heading: Clip In Climbing – NOW OPEN in Kwun Tong!
Beginners' Taster Session: 90 minutes with a qualified instructor; small groups of up to 6 people
Includes: safety talk, climbing shoe and harness hire, auto-belay walls and a low bouldering area
Price: $220 per person; students $180 (show your student card)
Opening hours: Monday to Friday 2 pm – 10 pm; Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays 10 am – 10 pm
Facilities: lockers, changing rooms, water refill station, small rest area with snacks for sale
Review form (OutThere HK): Your name / Date of visit / Title of your review
Rating icons (1 to 5 stars each): Staff | Safety | Price | Facilities

partB.role: a secondary student entering a competition
partB.audience: readers and judges of the youth magazine Stepping Out
partB.prompt: Many young adults in Hong Kong live with their parents until their late twenties or beyond. Stepping Out, a youth magazine, is holding an essay competition titled 'Living with your parents after you start work: a smart move?' Write an essay explaining why this is happening and arguing either that it is or that it is not a smart choice.

partB.role: a secondary student applying for a summer job
partB.audience: Ms Fong, Education Officer of the Hillcrest Museum of Childhood
partB.prompt: The Hillcrest Museum of Childhood in Hong Kong is looking for students aged 16 to 19 to work as summer guides. The guides will lead groups of visiting primary school children around the museum's new gallery of toys and games from Hong Kong's past. Write a letter to the museum's Education Officer, Ms Fong, applying for the job.

partB.role: a student asked by the Student Council to investigate
partB.prompt: Since the start of this school year, your school library has stayed open until 6.30 pm on weekdays. The Student Council has asked you to find out how students use the library after school. You have carried out a survey and observed the library for two weeks. Write a report for the Council presenting your findings and making recommendations.

A friend bet you that you could not get through a whole weekend without spending a single dollar. You accepted the bet. Write a blog post for your personal blog describing how your weekend went and what you learnt from it.
